ROUND 2 OF 2 (C34 FINAL) - PERFORMANCE: PASS-WITH-NOTES
PR: #311
Head: 5e03e0219a1a04fd3120355024bb72c28039a9de
Answers: 01a1fd56-a564-76c1-870e-fa169f622e9d

No performance correctness regression or demonstrated normal-use cost breach found. Round-one cost notes are substantially addressed: the R2 cost section explicitly prices total-event/payload fan-out, conditional inherited work, the existing counted /bin/ps fallback, and post-deploy AFTER debt. The new reconciliation closes the missing attach/gap trigger path without a timer or new launch site. This verdict does not replace the correctness review of B311-01.

Verified cost rows:

| Path | Work, frequency and scaling |
| --- | --- |
| Live subscriber | One daemon-wide receiver, not one per seat. Every broadcast Event is received/cloned before the kind filter, so CPU/allocation scales with total event rate and payload bytes, even when no lapse occurs. No unrelated-event SQL. Event-count retention uses the existing bounded ring (default capacity 1024), not a replay of the entire spine. |
| Delivered lapse | One outstanding() check, then the R1 exact-seat registry/liveness/conditional-remedy path only if the event sequence still matches. outstanding() is one latest_matching port call with THREE indexed LIMIT 1 seeks, a schema check and read-transaction setup/rollback, not one SQL statement. The three kinds are lapsed, renewed and seat.auth_recovery. |
| Reconcile | One registry.list filtered to live Copilot seats; the returned snapshot also includes live non-native Copilot seats, which are filtered in Rust. For N native seats: N latest_matching calls, hence 3N indexed tail seeks plus metadata/transaction work. Only an outstanding lapse reaches the existing decision path. Runs once on initial attachment and once per detected gap, never on a periodic tick. No full-spine history materialization. |
| Gap storm | One follower executes scans serially: concurrency is 1, with no per-gap task fan-out or backlog of scheduled rescans. Each replacement subscription starts with a fresh dropped counter, so a stale count cannot itself create an endless reattach loop. Another pass requires another observed gap in the new subscription. There is NO configured scans/second cap or cooldown. G gap recoveries cost G+1 roster passes and (G+1)*N latest_matching calls for a fixed N, plus conditional remedies. Unrelated broadcast traffic can cause those gaps. The 30-minute remedy budget does not limit these reads. |
| Closure/shutdown | Zero drops when the stream ends breaks the outer loop. Reattachment resets the count, avoiding a persistent old-gap retry loop. The daemon still aborts and joins the one follower task; the additive #309 spawn_waits field/stop integration retains extension_lost construction and shutdown wiring. No new shutdown poll or process launch was introduced by R2. |
| Liveness/remedy | Unchanged R1 path: kernel/procfs start observation normally launches nothing; the exceptional exact-PID /bin/ps path is absolute and records ps.proc-liveness-fallback. Existing pane reads/control delivery, CLI restart initialization, registration and notifications retain their conditional costs. No new launch site and no automatic revive. |

Sources at this head: auth_recovery.rs:567-694; events/mod.rs:259-283,459-492; store/spine.rs:64-65,367-395; store/registry.rs:447-471; core/config.rs:213. Liveness, tmux and latest_matching implementations are unchanged from R1; the merged registry addition is the separate #309 list_launched method, not a change to the list used here.

The lapse remains the POLICY input; reconciliation is another delivery path for that same input. outstanding(), process identity, idle/composer checks and the shared window are BRAKES, not new restart policies. The same follower cannot run its reconcile and live-event handler concurrently; the existing per-seat ledger lock continues to serialize concurrent F212 report admission.
